questions.question: You have 8 red blocks. You add 2 blue blocks. How many blocks do you have?
questions.explain: 8 + 2 makes 10. You already used the 2 to get to 10, so you do not add it again to get 12.

questions.question: You have 7 apples. You pick 3 more. How many apples do you have?
questions.explain: 7 + 3 makes 10. The 3 is already part of the 10, so you do not add it a second time to get 13.

questions.question: You have 6 fish in a bowl. 4 more swim in. How many fish do you have?
questions.explain: 6 + 4 makes 10. The 4 is already in the 10, so 14 is wrong. You just have 10 fish.

questions.question: You have 8 crayons. You get 3 more. How many crayons do you have?
questions.explain: Make 10 first: 8 + 2 = 10, then add the 1 left from the 3. So 10 + 1 = 11. Adding all 3 to the 10 gives 13, which is wrong.

questions.question: Mia has 7 cookies. Her mom bakes 5 more. How many cookies does Mia have now?
questions.explain: Make 10: 7 + 3 = 10, then add the 2 left from the 5. So 10 + 2 = 12. Adding all 5 to the 10 gives 15, which is wrong.

questions.question: You have 9 marbles. Your brother gives you 4 more. How many marbles do you have?
questions.explain: Make 10: 9 + 1 = 10, then add the 3 left. So 10 + 3 = 13. Adding all 4 to the 10 gives 14, which is wrong.

questions.question: What number do you add to 6 to make 10?
questions.explain: You need 4 because 6 + 4 = 10. Think: what goes with 6 to reach the 10? That is 4.

questions.question: You have 8 stickers. Your friend gives you 6 more. How many stickers do you have?
questions.explain: Make 10: 8 + 2 = 10, then add the 4 left from the 6. So 10 + 4 = 14. Adding all 6 to the 10 gives 16, which is wrong.

questions.question: You have 5 shells on the beach. You find some more and now have 11. How many more shells did you find?
questions.explain: You need 6 because 5 + 5 = 10, then 1 more makes 11. So 5 + 6 = 11. Forgetting the extra 1 gives you 5.

questions.question: Tom says 9 + 6 = 16. He did 10 + 6. Is Tom right?
questions.explain: 9 + 6: make 10 (9 + 1), then add 5 more to get 15. Tom added all 6, but he already used 1 of them to make the 10.

questions.question: You have 4 blocks. Your sister gives you some more. Now you have 10. How many did she give you?
questions.explain: 4 + 6 = 10. The partner of 4 to make 10 is 6. Picking 5 or 7 misses by one.

questions.question: You have 7 stamps. You need 12 to finish a set. How many more stamps do you need?
questions.explain: 7 + 3 = 10, then 2 more makes 12. So you need 5 more stamps. Picking 7 is wrong because that is where you started.
